laymanSummary: AOD-9604 is a **C-terminal fragment** of human growth hormone studied in *lipolysis (fat-metabolism)* research. It is investigated for effects on fat metabolism that are *proposed* to occur without activating the GH receptor or the IGF-1 growth pathway — used in research models where those axes need to be excluded as variables.
name: AOD-9604
shortDescription: hGH C-terminal fragment. Lipolysis research model; reported not to engage the GH receptor or IGF-1 axis. Lyophilized, 5mg vial.
longDescription:
AOD-9604 is the C-terminal fragment of human growth hormone (hGH176-191) modified with a tyrosine residue at position 176. Research applications center on lipolysis models where GH receptor activation and IGF-1 axis involvement must be excluded as variables. A β-3 adrenergic-linked lipolytic action has been proposed in preclinical work but is not firmly established; the fragment is reported not to bind the GH receptor. A Phase 2b human obesity trial did not meet its primary weight endpoint. Supplied as a lyophilized powder in a 5mg sealed vial.

Not for human use. For research purposes only.
mechanismSummary: C-terminal fragment of human growth hormone (hGH176-191) modified with a tyrosine at position 176. Studied in adipocyte lipolysis models; its precise molecular mechanism is not fully established. A β-3 adrenergic-linked lipolytic action has been proposed in preclinical work, and the fragment is reported not to bind the GH receptor or to raise IGF-1 levels. Note: a Phase 2 human obesity trial did not meet its primary weight endpoint.
receptorActivity: A selective β-3 adrenergic (ADRB3) lipolytic action has been proposed in preclinical models but is not firmly established for the intact fragment. Reported not to bind the GH receptor (GHR) or IGF-1R. Receptor-level interactions require further verification.
pathwaySummary: Proposed (not confirmed): β-3 adrenergic → Gs → cAMP → PKA → hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL) signaling in adipocytes, with reported independence from the GH receptor and IGF-1 axis. Specific downstream pathways for the fragment remain incompletely characterized in the literature.

laymanSummary: BPC-157 is a **body-protection peptide** first isolated from gastric juice, and it is the headliner of *tissue-repair research*. Animal models report **new blood-vessel formation** and ~accelerated repair of tendon, muscle, and gut tissue~. Unusually for a peptide it is *stable in gastric acid*, which is why it is so widely studied in gut and injury-recovery models.
name: BPC-157
shortDescription: Pentadecapeptide fragment of body protection compound. Angiogenic and regenerative research model. Lyophilized, 5mg vial.
longDescription:
BPC-157 is a 15-amino-acid peptide fragment derived from a protein found in human gastric juice. Research applications span tissue healing models, angiogenesis assays, and growth factor receptor upregulation studies. Stable in aqueous solution across a wide pH range. Supplied as a lyophilized powder in a 5mg sealed vial with certificate of analysis.

Not for human use. For research purposes only.
mechanismSummary: Pentadecapeptide fragment of body protection compound derived from human gastric juice. Promotes angiogenesis via VEGF receptor-2 upregulation, enhances growth factor receptor expression, and activates the FAK-paxillin pathway. Stable in aqueous solution under acidic and neutral pH — notable in vitro stability profile.
receptorActivity: Activates VEGF receptor-2 (VEGFR-2/KDR) and epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). Upregulates FAK-paxillin pathway and NO synthase signaling. No direct receptor binding identified for the intact pentadecapeptide; activity is primarily via growth factor receptor sensitization and downstream kinase cascades.
pathwaySummary: VEGFR-2 → PI3K/Akt/eNOS → NO production → endothelial cell proliferation and migration. FAK-paxillin → cytoskeletal reorganization for fibroblast and myoblast migration. Upregulates EGF and FGF receptor expression in target tissue.
fdaStatus: Not approved — preclinical / research use only

knownStudies.title: Stable gastric pentadecapeptide BPC 157: novel therapy in gastrointestinal tract
notes: Comprehensive review of 25+ years of BPC-157 preclinical research
Gastric ulcer healing, IBD models, gut-brain axis modulation documented
Stable in gastric acid — unique among peptide therapeutics

knownStudies.title: Achilles detachment in rat and stable gastric pentadecapeptide BPC 157: promoted tendon-to-bone healing and opposed corticosteroid aggravation
notes: Superior tendon insertion strength vs control at 4 and 8 weeks post-surgery
Enhanced collagen fiber alignment and reduced scar tissue at repair site

laymanSummary: CJC-1295 with **DAC** is a long-acting **GHRH** analogue — it signals the pituitary to release growth hormone, and an albumin-binding tag extends its action to a published estimate of *5.8–8.1 days*. Studies report ~sustained baseline GH and IGF-1 elevation~ rather than sharp spikes, and it is commonly investigated alongside a GHRP such as ipamorelin for additive signaling.
name: CJC-1295 DAC
shortDescription: GHRH analogue with Drug Affinity Complex albumin-binding technology. Lyophilized, 2mg vial.
longDescription:
CJC-1295 with Drug Affinity Complex (DAC) is a synthetic GHRH analogue with a maleimido-propionic acid group that forms a covalent bond with albumin cysteine-34 in vivo, with a published estimated half-life of 5.8–8.1 days. Used in GH axis research models where sustained GHRH-axis stimulation is required. Supplied as a lyophilized powder in a 2mg sealed vial with certificate of analysis.

Not for human use. For research purposes only.
mechanismSummary: GHRH analogue with Drug Affinity Complex (DAC) albumin-binding technology. The maleimido-propionic acid group forms a covalent bond with albumin cysteine-34; the published estimated half-life is 5.8–8.1 days. Maintains the sustained GH and IGF-1 axis stimulation profile of native GHRH without frequent dosing.
receptorActivity: GHRH receptor (GHRHR) agonist. The DAC modification forms a covalent bond to albumin Cys-34 without disrupting peptide–receptor interactions. Full agonism at GHRHR is maintained post-DAC conjugation.
pathwaySummary: GHRHR → Gs-coupled → adenylyl cyclase → cAMP → PKA → GH gene transcription and somatotroph Ca2+ sensitization. Sustained plasma levels from albumin binding extend the GHRH pulse without altering downstream GH/IGF-1 pathway mechanics.

laymanSummary: Epitalon is a four-amino-acid **pineal peptide** studied in *aging and circadian* research. In published studies it has been *reported to* ~activate telomerase~ — the enzyme that maintains the protective caps (telomeres) on chromosomes — and to influence melatonin rhythms. On that basis it is studied as a **circadian and cellular-aging** bioregulator. These findings derive largely from a limited number of research groups and warrant independent verification.
name: Epitalon
shortDescription: Tetrapeptide pineal peptide extract analogue. Telomerase activation, longevity research model. Lyophilized, 10mg vial.
longDescription:
Epitalon (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) is a synthetic tetrapeptide derived from the bovine pineal peptide preparation Epithalamin. Research applications include telomerase regulation studies, circadian biology models, and aging biology research. Reported to activate telomerase in somatic cells and upregulate pineal melatonin synthesis. Supplied as a lyophilized powder in a 10mg sealed vial.

Not for human use. For research purposes only.
mechanismSummary: Tetrapeptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) derived from the bovine pineal peptide preparation Epithalamin. Reported in preclinical studies to activate telomerase (hTERT) in somatic cells and to influence pineal melatonin synthesis via N-acetyltransferase. Research applications in cellular-aging, circadian-regulation, and neuroendocrine models. Independent replication of the telomerase findings remains limited.
receptorActivity: Reported to activate telomerase (hTERT) in somatic cells and to influence melatonin synthesis via pinealocyte N-acetyltransferase in preclinical models. No direct receptor has been identified for the intact tetrapeptide; proposed activity is attributed to intranuclear chromatin-modifying mechanisms and requires further verification.
pathwaySummary: hTERT (telomerase reverse transcriptase) activation → telomere elongation in somatic cells. Pineal N-acetyltransferase upregulation → melatonin synthesis restoration. Chromatin decondensation in aging cells → re-expression of silenced gene clusters.

laymanSummary: Ipamorelin is a **growth-hormone-releasing** peptide that acts on the pituitary to prompt an *endogenous GH pulse*. What makes it a research favorite is its **selectivity** — studies report ~GH release~ without the cortisol, prolactin, or appetite signaling seen with older peptides such as GHRP-6. It is short-acting, so it is used to model the *pulsatile* GH rhythm rather than continuous exposure.
name: Ipamorelin
shortDescription: Selective GHS-R1a agonist. No cortisol or prolactin elevation. Lyophilized, 5mg vial.
longDescription:
Ipamorelin is a selective pentapeptide growth hormone secretagogue receptor agonist (GHS-R1a). It stimulates pulsatile GH release from anterior pituitary somatotrophs with a high selectivity profile that avoids concurrent elevation of cortisol, prolactin, or ACTH. Supplied as a lyophilized powder in a 5mg sealed vial. Each lot is tested for purity by HPLC and ships with a certificate of analysis.

Not for human use. For research purposes only.
mechanismSummary: Selective GHS-R1a agonist that stimulates pulsatile GH release from anterior pituitary somatotrophs. High receptor selectivity distinguishes it from first-generation GHRPs. In the characterising study, ipamorelin released GH from primary rat pituitary cells with an EC50 of 1.3 ± 0.4 nmol/L, and did not release ACTH or cortisol at levels significantly different from GHRH stimulation.
receptorActivity: Selective GHS-R1a (growth hormone secretagogue receptor 1a) agonist. The characterising study reports no release of ACTH or cortisol above that seen with GHRH, and no effect on FSH, LH, prolactin or TSH. Note that the widely quoted 1.3 nmol/L figure is the EC50 for GH release from primary rat pituitary cells, not a GHS-R1a receptor-binding constant.
pathwaySummary: GHS-R1a → Gq-coupled → IP3/DAG/PKC cascade → somatotroph intracellular Ca2+ release → GH secretory granule exocytosis. Independent of the GHRH axis; acts via a distinct intracellular signaling cascade that permits additive GH secretion when combined with GHRH analogues.

knownStudies.title: Ipamorelin, the first selective growth hormone secretagogue
notes: Full GHS-R1a agonist profile characterized
No ACTH, cortisol, or prolactin elevation at GH-stimulating doses
Distinct selectivity vs GHRP-2 and GHRP-6 analogs

knownStudies.title: Pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic modeling of ipamorelin, a growth hormone releasing peptide, in human volunteers
notes: Confirmed dose-dependent GH secretion in humans
No HPA axis activation confirmed at all doses tested
Favorable safety profile with no dose-limiting toxicity

laymanSummary: KPV is a three-amino-acid tail of the **α-MSH** hormone with outsized **anti-inflammatory** activity in research models. It is reported to ~downregulate NF-κB inflammatory signaling~ and is studied in *gut inflammation, IBD, and wound-healing* models. Notably, the published work indicates it works *without* engaging the melanocortin receptors its parent hormone acts on — so it carries the anti-inflammatory activity without the pigmentation signaling.
name: KPV
shortDescription: α-MSH C-terminal tripeptide. NF-κB suppression, anti-inflammatory research model. Lyophilized, 10mg vial.
longDescription:
KPV is the C-terminal tripeptide (Lys-Pro-Val) of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH). Research applications include inflammatory bowel disease models, wound healing assays, and systemic inflammatory response studies. Reported to suppress NF-κB signaling through a melanocortin-receptor-independent route involving PepT1-mediated uptake. Supplied as a lyophilized powder in a 10mg sealed vial.

Not for human use. For research purposes only.
mechanismSummary: C-terminal tripeptide of α-MSH (Lys-Pro-Val). Reported to suppress NF-κB and MAP kinase inflammatory signaling and to inhibit neutrophil recruitment. Preclinical work indicates uptake via the peptide transporter PepT1 and describes the anti-inflammatory effect as melanocortin-receptor-independent. Research applications in colitis, wound healing, and systemic inflammatory models.
receptorActivity: No established melanocortin receptor activity: preclinical studies report that the KPV anti-inflammatory effect persists when MC1R is non-functional and is not blocked by melanocortin antagonists, and that KPV does not raise cAMP. Reported activity is attributed to PepT1-mediated uptake followed by antagonism of NF-κB nuclear translocation rather than to receptor binding.
pathwaySummary: Proposed: PepT1-mediated cellular uptake → inhibition of NF-κB nuclear translocation and MAP kinase signaling → reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine transcription. Inhibition of neutrophil and macrophage recruitment at inflammatory foci has been reported in preclinical models.

laymanSummary: Pinealon is a short **Glu-Asp-Arg** (EDR) tripeptide developed as a pineal-gland **bioregulator**. It is studied in research contexts for **neuronal protection, cognitive function, and circadian regulation** — a distinct compound from the tetrapeptide Epitalon.
mechanismSummary: Synthetic tripeptide (Glu-Asp-Arg, also written EDR). Investigated as a short-peptide bioregulator in neuroprotection, cognitive-function, and circadian-regulation research models. Proposed mechanisms involve tissue-specific regulation of gene expression; a single validated receptor target has not been established for the intact tripeptide.
receptorActivity: No single validated receptor target has been established for the intact Glu-Asp-Arg tripeptide. Reported activity is attributed to short-peptide bioregulator mechanisms in preclinical models rather than to a defined receptor interaction.
pathwaySummary: Proposed short-peptide bioregulator activity in neuronal and circadian research models. Specific downstream pathways for the intact tripeptide are not well characterized and warrant further verification before any mechanistic claim is published.
name: Pinealon
shortDescription: Tri-peptide pineal bioregulator (Glu-Asp-Arg). 5mg lyophilized vial.
longDescription:
Pinealon is a short synthetic tri-peptide (Glu-Asp-Arg) developed by Khavinson et al. as a pineal-gland bioregulator for research into neuronal protection, cognitive function, and circadian regulation.

Supplied as lyophilized powder in a sealed vial for laboratory reconstitution. Not for human use. For research purposes only.

name: Retatrutide
shortDescription: Triple GIP/GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonist. Lyophilized, 5mg vial.
longDescription:
Retatrutide supplied as a lyophilized powder in a single 5mg vial. Intended strictly for laboratory and in-vitro research applications. Each lot is tested for purity by HPLC and ships sealed with a certificate of analysis on request.

Not for human use. For research purposes only.
laymanSummary: Retatrutide is an investigational **triple receptor agonist** that activates the **GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon** receptors together. In published *Phase 2 clinical research*, a mean body-weight reduction of approximately ~24%~ was reported over 48 weeks — among the largest reported for this class. The three receptor pathways are studied for their combined effects on *appetite signaling*, *glucose regulation*, and *energy expenditure*.
mechanismSummary: Triple GIP/GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonist. The glucagon component is reported to reduce hepatic glucose output and to augment weight loss through glucagon-receptor-mediated increases in energy expenditure, adding to the dual GIP/GLP-1 axis.
receptorActivity: Agonist at GIP-R, GLP-1R and GCGR. The characterising study describes balanced GCGR and GLP-1R activity with greater GIP-R activity. Published potency values for the three receptors could not be verified against an accessible primary table and are therefore not stated here.
pathwaySummary: Incretin axis (GIP + GLP-1): insulin secretion amplification, satiety signaling. Glucagon axis (GCGR): hepatic glucose output reduction and increased energy expenditure. The cellular basis of the energy-expenditure effect is not settled in the literature.
fdaStatus: Investigational — Phase 3 program ongoing; not FDA approved

−17.5% at 4 mg and −22.8% at 8 mg, 48 weeks
100% of 12 mg cohort achieved ≥5% weight loss; 83% ≥15%; 63% ≥20%
Appetite suppression and reduced caloric intake observed

−2.02% HbA1c at 12 mg vs −0.01% placebo

notes: ~17% body weight reduction in diet-induced obese mice
Increased energy expenditure and improved glucose tolerance
Balanced triple-receptor agonism characterized in vitro

notes: −8.96% mean body weight and −1.42% HbA1c at 12 mg, 12 weeks
Dose-dependent glucose lowering
Acceptable safety and tolerability profile

laymanSummary: Semaglutide is a **GLP-1 receptor agonist** that mimics a gut hormone released after eating. It is investigated for effects on *appetite signaling*, *gastric emptying*, and *glucose regulation*. In published *Phase 3 clinical trials*, a mean body-weight reduction of approximately ~15%~ was reported. A fatty-acid chain gives it a half-life of about a week.
name: Semaglutide
shortDescription: Research-grade GLP-1 receptor agonist peptide. Lyophilized, 5mg vial.
longDescription:
Research-grade Semaglutide peptide supplied as a lyophilized powder in a single 5mg vial. Intended strictly for laboratory and in-vitro research applications. Each lot is tested for purity by HPLC and ships sealed with a certificate of analysis on request.

Not for human use. For research purposes only.
mechanismSummary: GLP-1 receptor agonist with high affinity for GLP-1R. Mediates glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon, and delays gastric emptying. A C18 fatty di-acid attached at Lys26 via a hydrophilic γGlu-2×AEEA spacer mediates albumin binding, extending elimination half-life to approximately 1 week and enabling once-weekly dosing.
receptorActivity: Primary: GLP-1R (high affinity; reported binding affinity is reduced relative to liraglutide, and is markedly lower in the presence of albumin — the condition that matters in vivo). No meaningful activity at GIP-R, GCGR, or other incretin receptors at physiological concentrations.
pathwaySummary: GLP-1R → cAMP/PKA/CREB cascade → glucose-dependent potentiation of pancreatic β-cell insulin exocytosis. Hypothalamic arcuate nucleus satiety circuit activation via vagal afferents and central GLP-1R expression.

knownStudies.title: Once-Weekly Semaglutide in Adults with Overweight or Obesity (STEP 1)
notes: n=1,961 adults, 68-week trial
14.9% mean body weight reduction vs 2.4% placebo
50.5% of participants lost ≥15% body weight at max dose

knownStudies.title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes (SUSTAIN-6)
notes: n=3,297 participants, 104-week trial
26% reduction in composite MACE endpoint vs placebo
Non-fatal stroke RRR: 39%

knownStudies.title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Obesity Without Diabetes (SELECT)
notes: n=17,604 non-diabetic patients with established CVD
20% reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events
First trial to show CV benefit in non-diabetic obesity population

appearance: Semaglutide is a white to almost white hygroscopic powder (FDA prescribing information, Ozempic).

laymanSummary: Semax is a Russian-developed **nootropic** peptide built from a fragment of ACTH. Research models report ~elevated BDNF and NGF~ — the brain's own growth factors — which is why it is studied against *attention, memory, and neuroprotection* endpoints. It is also investigated in stroke models, where its small size and *intranasal* route are studied for CNS access.
name: Semax
shortDescription: ACTH(4-7) Pro-Gly-Pro analogue. BDNF/NGF upregulation, cognitive research model. Lyophilized, 30mg vial.
longDescription:
Semax is a synthetic analogue of the ACTH(4-7) peptide fragment with a Pro-Gly-Pro C-terminal extension that confers resistance to enzymatic degradation. Research applications include neurotrophic factor regulation models, cognitive function studies, and neuroprotective assays. Upregulates BDNF, NGF, and VEGF expression in cortical and hippocampal tissue preparations. Supplied as a lyophilized powder in a 30mg sealed vial.

Not for human use. For research purposes only.
mechanismSummary: ACTH(4-7) Pro-Gly-Pro analogue with enhanced enzymatic stability. The C-terminal Pro-Gly-Pro extension is reported to confer resistance to enzymatic degradation. Studied for upregulation of BDNF, NGF, and VEGF expression in cortical and hippocampal tissue. Investigated via intranasal and parenteral routes in central nervous system research models.
receptorActivity: No direct binding at classical neuroreceptor subtypes. Reported activity is attributed to upregulation of endogenous BDNF and NGF expression and of TrkB, rather than to direct receptor binding by the peptide itself.
pathwaySummary: Proposed: elevated BDNF/TrkB expression → Ras/MAPK/ERK → CREB → pro-survival gene transcription. Modulation of dopaminergic and serotonergic tone has also been reported in preclinical models. Specific downstream pathways remain incompletely characterized.

laymanSummary: TB-500 is a synthetic form of **thymosin β4**, a repair-associated protein distributed widely through tissue. It acts on the cell's internal scaffolding (**actin**), and research models report ~cell migration toward injury sites~, ~new blood-vessel formation~, and ~reduced scar formation~. A staple of *regeneration and recovery research*, often studied alongside BPC-157.
name: TB-500
shortDescription: Synthetic thymosin β4 analogue. Actin polymerization, tissue repair research. Lyophilized, 5mg vial.
longDescription:
TB-500 is a synthetic analogue of the naturally occurring peptide thymosin β4. Research applications span musculoskeletal repair models, cardiac tissue studies, and directed cell migration assays. Acts via G-actin sequestration and activation of PI3K/Akt survival pathways. Supplied as a lyophilized powder in a 5mg sealed vial with certificate of analysis.

Not for human use. For research purposes only.
mechanismSummary: Synthetic peptide analogue of thymosin β4. Upregulates the actin-sequestering G-actin pool, promotes endothelial and smooth muscle cell migration, and activates PI3K/Akt survival pathways. Investigated in cardiac and musculoskeletal repair models. Acts primarily via cytoskeletal reorganization rather than classical receptor-ligand binding.
receptorActivity: Acts via G-actin sequestration rather than classical receptor–ligand binding. Reported in preclinical models to activate Akt/protein kinase B and ILK (integrin-linked kinase) and to upregulate matrix metalloproteinase-2 for extracellular matrix remodeling. Primary effect is cytoskeletal.
pathwaySummary: PI3K/Akt/ILK → inhibition of apoptosis, activation of cell survival. G-actin sequestration promotes lamellipodia formation and directed cell migration. MMP-2 upregulation for basement membrane remodeling in tissue repair contexts.

laymanSummary: Tirzepatide is a **dual GIP + GLP-1 receptor agonist**. Activating **two incretin receptors together** is investigated for effects on *appetite signaling* and *glucose and lipid metabolism* beyond GLP-1 alone. In head-to-head *Phase 3 clinical trials*, a mean body-weight reduction of up to ~22%~ was reported, greater than semaglutide in the study population. A half-life of about a week places it in the long-acting class.
name: Tirzepatide
shortDescription: Dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist peptide. Lyophilized, 10mg vial.
longDescription:
Tirzepatide supplied as a lyophilized powder in a single 10mg vial. Intended strictly for laboratory and in-vitro research applications. Each lot is tested for purity by HPLC and ships sealed with a certificate of analysis on request.

Not for human use. For research purposes only.
mechanismSummary: Dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist. The characterising study reports greater in-vitro potency at the GIP receptor than at the GLP-1 receptor. GIP component enhances incretin amplification and adipocyte lipid metabolism; GLP-1 component mediates gastric emptying inhibition and central satiety signaling.
receptorActivity: Agonist at GIP-R and GLP-1R, with greater reported in-vitro potency at GIP-R; the characterising study describes GLP-1R potency as approximately 13-fold weaker than native GLP-1. Dual coagonism without significant glucagon receptor activity.
pathwaySummary: GIP-R → cAMP/PKA axis in pancreatic β-cells and adipocytes, PI3K/Akt in fat tissue. GLP-1R → cAMP/EPAC/PKA, hypothalamic satiety (arcuate nucleus), gastric motility suppression via vagal pathways.

Up to 2.4% HbA1c reduction at 15mg dose

Sterile 0.6% acetic acid solution for laboratory reconstitution of peptides that require an acidic carrier (BPC-157, TB-500, and similar). Supplied in a 3 mL sealed glass vial with rubber septum.

longDescription:
Sterile bacteriostatic water suitable for laboratory reconstitution of lyophilized peptides and other research compounds. Preserved with 0.9% benzyl alcohol for multi-dose use. Supplied in a 30mL sealed glass vial with rubber septum.

Individually packaged, sterile 1mL research syringes with a fixed 29G × 1/2″ needle. Graduated in U-100 units for precise laboratory dosing. Latex-free. One hundred syringes per box.

Not for human use. For research purposes only.

laymanSummary: Adamax is a **synthetic analog of Semax** — the ACTH-derived nootropic peptide — modified with an *adamantyl group and N-terminal acetylation*. Those changes are *intended* to extend the peptide's stability and improve how well it crosses the blood-brain barrier, so it is investigated in the same *cognitive, neuroprotective, and stress-response* areas as Semax. Note that no published study of this specific analogue could be located — its properties are inferred from the Semax scaffold rather than measured.
name: Adamax
shortDescription: Adamantylated, N-acetylated Semax analog. Nootropic/neuroprotective research model. Lyophilized, 10mg vial.
longDescription:
Adamax is a synthetic analog of the nootropic peptide Semax (an ACTH(4-7) Pro-Gly-Pro derivative), modified by N-terminal acetylation and the addition of an adamantyl moiety. These modifications are intended to increase metabolic stability and blood-brain-barrier penetration relative to unmodified Semax; no primary literature characterising the pharmacokinetics of this analogue could be located, and those properties should be treated as unverified. Research applications parallel those of Semax: neurotrophic signaling, cognitive function models, neuroprotection, and stress-response biology. Supplied as a lyophilized powder in a 10mg sealed vial.

Not for human use. For research purposes only.
mechanismSummary: Adamantyl- and N-acetyl-modified analog of Semax (ACTH(4-7) Pro-Gly-Pro). The adamantyl group and acetylation are intended to confer resistance to enzymatic degradation and improve blood-brain-barrier penetration; these properties are not established in primary literature for this analogue. Studied for the BDNF/NGF-related neurotrophic signaling associated with the Semax scaffold.
receptorActivity: No direct binding at classical neuroreceptor subtypes reported; proposed activity is attributed to the Semax scaffold — stimulation of endogenous BDNF/NGF expression — with the adamantyl and N-acetyl modifications proposed to extend exposure. No primary literature characterising this analogue could be located; receptor-level activity is unverified.
pathwaySummary: Proposed, by analogy to the Semax scaffold: elevated BDNF/TrkB expression → Ras/MAPK/ERK → CREB → pro-survival gene transcription. Pathway activity has not been characterised for this analogue specifically.
